title: U.S. House · Texas's 10th District
area: A redrawn district running from the Austin area northeast toward Bryan-College Station in central Texas.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Michael McCaul (R) retired from public office rather than seek re-election following Texas's August 2025 congressional redistricting. Caitlin Rourk won a three-candidate Democratic primary; Chris Gober won a multi-candidate Republican primary.

summary.text: Caitlin Rourk is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 10th District. According to her campaign website, she is a U.S. Army officer and mother whose career spans communications and public policy work, Army National Guard and Reserve service, and a role at Dell Technologies. She is campaigning on affordable health care, economic opportunity and public schools.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she was raised by public school teachers, and both of her grandfathers served in World War II.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Chicago and an MBA from the McCombs School of Business at the University of Texas at Austin.

Earned a commission as a Military Intelligence Officer through the U.S. Army Officer Candidate School and served full time in the Texas Army National Guard at Joint Forces Headquarters in Austin, where, her website says, she supported responses to natural disasters, COVID-19, civil unrest operations and border mobilizations. She also served in the U.S. Army Reserve.

Her website says her early career involved working across party lines on policy issues ranging from energy security to deficit reduction; her most recent private-sector job was leading communications at Dell Technologies.
Has not previously held elected office; won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary for the open 10th District seat.

According to her campaign website, she has lived, worked and served in Central Texas for more than a decade and lives in the district with her husband, a volunteer EMT and medic who served in the Texas State Guard, and their two young children.

priorities.text: Affordable, accessible healthcare: lower drug costs, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, expand mental health care and strengthen the ACA.
Economic opportunity: raise and index the federal minimum wage to the cost of living, expand affordable child care, and protect and strengthen Social Security.

positions.summary: Says she will work to lower drug costs, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions and strengthen the Affordable Care Act.
Lists a 'living minimum wage' among her economic priorities.
Lists affordable child care among her priorities for the district.
Says economic policy 'too often' favors the wealthy and well-connected and that she will hold corporations accountable to pay 'their fair share.'

summary.text: Chris Gober is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 10th District. An attorney and business owner, he built a conservative election-law practice and in 2024 was director and chief lawyer of America PAC, a super PAC founded by Elon Musk that supported Donald Trump's presidential campaign. His campaign website describes him as the Trump-endorsed candidate and lists border security, opposing what it calls the weaponization of government, and economic growth among his priorities.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a seventh-generation Texan who was born and raised in the Texas towns of Throckmorton and Graham, and he now lives in Austin with his wife and two daughters.
Graduated from Texas A&M University in 2001 and Harvard Law School in 2004.

Worked on national-security and border-security issues at the U.S. Department of Justice and then served as a top lawyer for the Republican Party, according to his campaign website; his Ballotpedia survey response places the party role with the Republican Party of Texas.
Founded a conservative law practice after returning to Texas. His campaign website says he started it with $10,000 in savings and that his businesses now employ more than 50 people across 17 states.

Says he represented conservative nonprofit groups in a case against the IRS over its tax-exempt rules and won a ruling striking down the regulation, and that he won a U.S. Supreme Court case for Sen. Ted Cruz challenging a provision of the Federal Election Campaign Act.

In 2024, served as director and chief lawyer of America PAC, which he says deployed nearly $300 million supporting Donald Trump's presidential campaign; he also says he defended the PAC and Elon Musk in lawsuits.

Says he helped establish the America First Policy Institute and helped deliver a Republican redistricting plan. He has not previously held elected office; he advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Secure the border and reduce illegal immigration, crime and drug trafficking, working with the Trump administration.
Oppose what he describes as the 'weaponization' of federal agencies against conservatives.

Says he will cut regulations, expand small-business opportunities, and strengthen rural healthcare access for rural Texans; also calls for AI-infrastructure policy that protects rural electricity rates and local water supplies from large data-center projects.

positions.summary: Says he will work with President Trump to 'secure our border and crush the cartels' by enforcing immigration laws and empowering Texas law enforcement.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has held elected office, so there is no official voting or legislative record to report. Biographical details for both candidates come mainly from their own campaign materials and Ballotpedia profiles; no independent news profile was reviewed.
